Report BH-adjusted p-values as the significance criterion; do not report nominal p-value counts as if they were significant findings

steps.name: Per-subject consistency and method cross-check
caveats: Per-subject deltas from VST data are descriptive; they carry no per-gene p-value and must not be presented as a per-subject significance test
limma-voom with n=10 and 4 residual degrees of freedom after blocking is itself underpowered; disagreement between methods at the margin is expected
Sign concordance across 5 pairs has a one-in-sixteen chance under a null of random direction, so full concordance alone is weak evidence without the FDR-controlled statistic beside it
steps.context: The research question asks which genes respond within each subject, so the per-pair behaviour is part of the answer, not an afterthought. With 5 pairs a single outlying subject can drive a low p-value, and the paired DESeq2 table alone does not expose that. A second method with a different set of distributional assumptions provides a sensitivity check on the gene list rather than a second, independent p-value.
steps.question: For the genes called responsive to treatment, does the treated-minus-control change hold in the same direction across all five subjects, or is it driven by a minority of pairs — and does an independent paired method recover the same genes?
constraints: Use the same filtered gene set and the same subject-blocked design across all three methods so the comparison is like-for-like
Do not present the three methods as independent confirmation — they share the same 10 samples; frame the agreement as method-sensitivity, not replication
Report genes whose signal comes from fewer than 4 of the 5 pairs as pair-driven and unreliable, regardless of their padj
steps.description: From the VST matrix and sample table produced in T1S1, compute for every retained gene the per-subject paired difference (treated minus control) in each of the 5 subjects, giving a genes x 5 delta matrix. For each gene report the number of subjects moving in the same direction as the overall shrunk LFC from T1S2, the median and interquartile range of the per-subject deltas, and a simple consistency flag (e.g. all 5 pairs concordant in sign). Annotate the T1S2 results table with these consistency statistics and write the merged table. Produce a heatmap of the per-subject delta matrix for the top-ranked genes, and per-gene paired line plots (control to treated, one line per subject) for the top 20 by padj. Paired limma-voom and paired edgeR quasi-likelihood analyses with subject blocking are both run and their statistics compared to DESeq2 by rank correlation and top-list overlap

caveats: Enrichment on a ranking derived from 5 pairs reflects a weak underlying signal; report NES and q-values without inflating them into mechanistic claims

Whole-blood expression is strongly shaped by cell-composition shifts, so immune/inflammatory pathway enrichment may reflect a change in leukocyte proportions rather than transcriptional regulation within a cell type — state this alternative explanation
Hallmark sets are broad and overlapping; a significant hallmark is a direction to look, not a mechanism
steps.context: Consumes the full ranked gene list from the paired DESeq2 fit in T1S2 (all tested genes, ranked by shrunk log2 fold change or by the signed Wald statistic). Set-level testing borrows strength across genes and is the appropriate readout when a 5-pair gene-level test has limited power. The counts matrix is keyed on HGNC gene symbols and the organism is Homo sapiens, so human symbol-based gene sets are required.
steps.question: Which biological processes shift coherently with treatment across the 5 paired blood samples, even where individual genes fall short of FDR significance?
constraints: Use human gene sets — the data is Homo sapiens; a mouse or rat collection would produce meaningless results
Ties and duplicate gene symbols in the ranking must be handled explicitly (report duplicates and how they were resolved) before ranking
If either gene set collection is unavailable in the environment, report which one is missing and proceed with the one that is present rather than substituting a different organism or collection
steps.description: Load the complete ranked gene list from T1S2 (every tested gene, not a thresholded subset), ranking by the signed Wald statistic with the shrunk log2 fold change as an alternative ranking reported for sensitivity. Human hallmark and human GO biological process gene sets are used, with the organism and symbol identifier space verified before scoring, and the gene-to-set match rate reported

Redundant GO sets are collapsed before any count of significant pathways is reported

plan.title: Paired treated-vs-control DE in 5 subjects
plan.analytical_narrative:
The input is a single bulk RNA-seq count matrix (counts.csv, 12,000 gene symbols x 11 columns: gene-symbol column plus 10 sample columns) with metadata.csv giving 10 rows and 3 columns (sample, subject, condition). The design is explicitly paired: 5 subjects, each contributing one control and one treated sample. The research question — which genes respond to treatment within each subject — is therefore a within-subject (paired) differential expression question, and the analysis must block on subject rather than treat the 10 samples as independent. With n=5 pairs the paired design is the main source of power: subject-level baseline differences in blood transcriptomes are typically the largest variance component, and removing them via a ~ subject + condition design is what makes a treatment effect detectable at all.

T1S1 loads counts and metadata, verifies the sample columns match the metadata rows and that every subject has exactly one control and one treated sample, filters low-count genes (edgeR filterByExpr on the paired design), and produces normalized/VST-transformed expression plus paired-structure diagnostics (PCA coloured by subject and by condition, within-pair correlation, library sizes). This step establishes whether subject truly dominates the variance — the empirical justification for the blocked design — and flags any sample whose pairing looks broken.

T1S2 runs the primary test: DESeq2 with design ~ subject + condition (subject as a blocking factor, condition as the tested coefficient), Wald test on the treated-vs-control contrast, LFC shrinkage for ranking, and BH FDR. This is the direct answer to the question. Because it is exactly the comparison that is underpowered at n=5, the step must also report the unpaired (~ condition) result side by side so the gain from pairing is quantified rather than assumed, and must report how many genes pass FDR thresholds honestly, including the possibility that none do.

T1S3 is the per-subject view the question also asks for: paired log2 ratios (treated - control) computed per subject from the normalized data, so a reader can see whether a gene called significant moves consistently in all five subjects or is driven by one or two. Consistency counts and per-subject heatmaps are reported alongside a limma-voom with duplicateCorrelation / paired-limma cross-check as a method-sensitivity check on the DESeq2 gene list. No gene should be reported as a treatment responder on the strength of a single subject.

T2S1 takes the ranked gene list into pathway space with GSEA on the full shrunk-LFC ranking (not just the significant subset, which may be empty) against the staged human hallmark and GO-BP gene sets, matched to Homo sapiens and HGNC symbols as the counts file uses gene symbols. Set-level testing is the appropriate fallback when a 5-pair gene-level test has little power, and it is framed that way — a coherent pathway shift with no individually significant gene is a real and reportable outcome.
